title: Advanced Analytics
tagline: Multi-level rollups, share-of-total, cohorts and funnels

placementQuiz.q: Which computes every subset-combination of grouped columns for multi-dimensional analysis?
placementQuiz.explain: GROUPING SETS lets you request specific grouping combinations; CUBE/ROLLUP are its conveniences.

placementQuiz.q: A result row belongs to the grand-total set. What best identifies the non-grouped rows produced by a rollup?
placementQuiz.explain: GROUPING(col) returns 1 when col is collapsed by the rollup, distinguishing rollup NULLs from real NULLs.

placementQuiz.q: Which is a correct share-of-total pattern?
placementQuiz.explain: Dividing by a window SUM without a frame — SUM(value) OVER () — yields the grand total per row.

placementQuiz.q: A day-N retention table keys each cohort by first_activity_date. What is the retention ratio for a cell?
placementQuiz.explain: Cohort size from the first-period count; later periods' surviving users divided by it.

placementQuiz.q: In a funnel you must preserve one row per user and know the deepest step reached. Which tool fits?
placementQuiz.explain: Rank each user's step events, then aggregate the rank to the deepest completed step per user.

blocks.md: A rollup answers many questions from one scan; a funnel and a cohort answer product questions in a language executives already speak. Learn the shapes, not the tools.

`GROUPING SETS ((region, dept), (region), ())` asks for exactly the subtotal groupings you need, in one pass. `ROLLUP (region, dept)` is shorthand for a hierarchy — finest grain up to the grand total. `CUBE (a, b)` is every subset combination, margins included. In the output a collapsed dimension shows as NULL, and `GROUPING(col)` reports 1 exactly when `col` was rolled away — the only reliable way to tell a subtotal NULL from a real NULL.

blocks.label: grouping sets
blocks.code:
SELECT region,
       dept,
       SUM(amount)       AS revenue,
       GROUPING(region)  AS r_bucket,
       GROUPING(dept)    AS d_bucket
FROM orders
GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((region, dept), (region), ());
blocks.pg: -- PostgreSQL: GROUPING SETS / ROLLUP / CUBE are core SQL
blocks.mysql: -- MySQL 8.0: ROLLUP only (no CUBE, no GROUPING SETS); GROUPING() is supported
blocks.py-pandas: # pandas: groupby per level then concat, or use subtotal=False pivot_table margins

blocks.label: rollup variant
blocks.code:
SELECT region,
       dept,
       SUM(amount)      AS revenue,
       GROUPING(region) AS r_bucket,
       GROUPING(dept)   AS d_bucket
FROM orders
GROUP BY ROLLUP (region, dept)
ORDER BY region NULLS LAST, dept NULLS LAST;
blocks.mysql: -- MySQL 8.0: GROUP BY region, dept WITH ROLLUP + GROUPING()

items.q: GROUP BY ROLLUP (region, dept) generates which groupings?
options: A cross join of regions and depts
items.explain: ROLLUP follows column order: (region, dept) → (region) → (), never the (dept)-only margin — that is CUBE's job.

items.q: Why do rollup results end with NULL region rows?
options: Because regions are literally named NULL
The subtotal rows collapse region, and GROUPING() tells them apart
items.explain: Rollup leaves the collapsed column NULL in subtotal rows; GROUPING(region)=1 flags those rows so real NULL regions stay distinguishable.

blocks.label: share + delta
blocks.code:
SELECT day,
       SUM(amount) AS revenue,
       SUM(amount) / SUM(SUM(amount)) OVER () AS share_of_all,
       SUM(amount) - LAG(SUM(amount)) OVER (ORDER BY day) AS day_delta
FROM orders
GROUP BY day
ORDER BY day;
blocks.pg: -- The window runs AFTER grouping: SUM(SUM(amount)) OVER () = grand total
blocks.mysql: -- MySQL 8.0: window functions over grouped output work the same

blocks.label: period over period %
blocks.code:
SELECT day,
       SUM(amount) AS revenue,
       ROUND(100.0 * (SUM(amount) - LAG(SUM(amount)) OVER (ORDER BY day))
              / NULLIF(LAG(SUM(amount)) OVER (ORDER BY day), 0), 2) AS pct_delta
FROM orders
GROUP BY day
ORDER BY day;

blocks.md: A window function over a GROUP BY result partitions the **aggregate output**, not the raw rows. The double SUM — `SUM(SUM(amount)) OVER ()` — re-sums the group totals, which is exactly the grand total of revenue. Never write `SUM(amount) / SUM(amount)`; after grouping there is no scalar `amount` left, and a naive re-sum would collapse to 1.

items.q: Why is SUM(amount)/SUM(SUM(amount)) OVER () correct but SUM(amount)/SUM(amount) wrong?
options: The window needs the grouped aggregate, so you re-sum the aggregate output
SUM(amount) is undefined after GROUP BY
The outer SUM must be a percentage
items.explain: After GROUP BY, the window must sum the grouped totals — SUM(SUM(amount)) OVER () — not re-sum the same column, which would collapse each row to 1.

items.q: The share-of-total column uses OVER () with no frame or partition. What does it compute?
options: A running total up to each day
The grand total across all days
items.explain: With no ORDER BY, the window frame is the whole grouped set, so the window SUM equals the grand total — the denominator every share needs.

blocks.md: A **cohort** is a group of users sharing a first-activity date — their acquisition period. Retention asks: of the users acquired in period P, how many are still active in period P+n? The **funnel** counts, per user, how deep they got through an ordered step sequence (signup → cart → purchase) within a single path.

blocks.label: retention over time
blocks.code:
WITH first_orders AS (
  SELECT user_id, MIN(order_date)::date AS first_day
  FROM orders
  GROUP BY user_id
)
SELECT f.first_day AS cohort,
       (o.order_date::date - f.first_day) AS days_since,
       COUNT(DISTINCT o.user_id) AS retained
FROM first_orders f
JOIN orders o ON o.user_id = f.user_id
GROUP BY 1, 2;
blocks.pg: -- MIN(order_date) per user defines the cohort bucket (date - date = integer days)
blocks.mysql: -- MySQL 8.0: replace ::date casts with DATE(...); DATEDIFF(o.order_date, f.first_day)

blocks.label: funnel by rank
blocks.code:
WITH steps AS (
  SELECT user_id, event, ts,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts) AS step_rank
  FROM events
  WHERE event IN ('signup', 'cart', 'purchase')
)
SELECT event,
       COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS users
FROM steps
GROUP BY event
ORDER BY MIN(step_rank);
blocks.pg: -- step_rank orders each user's own path; MIN(step_rank) keeps the canonical step order

items.q: Why is cohort membership defined with MIN(order_date) per user?
options: First purchase date sets the cohort period the user is attributed to
Because order_date is an index key
items.explain: Cohorts key on first activity; MIN(order_date) per user IS their first-purchase date, and every later period is measured against it.

items.q: Why does the funnel rank events with per-user step_rank instead of comparing absolute timestamps across users?
options: Rank orders each user's own sequence, so step order is per-user
It avoids a JOIN to sessions
items.explain: ROW_NUMBER() PARTITION BY user_id sequences each user's own path; absolute clock times cannot tell a quick buyer from a multi-session window shopper.

blocks.md: A single HashAggregate computes every requested grouping set in one pass over `orders` — rollup does not rescan the table per subtotal level. The planner may add a trailing Sort when the query demands an order (e.g. `ORDER BY region NULLS LAST, dept NULLS LAST`), which is why rollups keep one-pass cost but still pay a final sort for human-readable output.

items.q: How many passes over orders does a single ROLLUP normally need?
options: One HashAggregate pass for all sets, plus maybe a final sort
Two: one to count, one to order
One per view in the FROM clause
items.explain: GROUPING SETS/ROLLUP/CUBE execute as one aggregation pass; ordering is applied afterwards only when requested.

blocks.subtitle: Rollups, shares, cohorts and funnels — interview-shaped drills.

items.title: Quarterly Rollup Report
items.statement: Write a quarterly revenue report with a total row: ROLLUP over quarter with the GROUPING() mask and NULLS LAST ordering.
hints: GROUPING(quarter) AS total_row, ORDER BY quarter NULLS LAST

items.title: Grouping-Set Breakdown
items.statement: Produce segment totals plus overall totals in one query: revenue grouped by (country, device), by (country), and by the empty set (), all in a single scan.

items.title: Share with Rollup Included
items.statement: Extend a ROLLUP(region, dept) query with a share-of-total column computed as a window function over the whole grouped set, so the grand-total row shows 100%.

items.title: Week-Over-Week Delta
items.statement: Compute week-over-week revenue and percent change, aligning ISO weeks so Monday compares to the previous Monday.
hints: date_trunc('week', order_date)::date as iso_week, then LAG over it

items.title: Retention Matrix
items.statement: Build a cohort × week retention table: cohort = first_activity week, cells = ROUND(retained / cohort_size) percentages for week 0..4.
hints: MIN(first_activity) as cohort; count survivors per cohort-week

items.title: Step Funnel Counts
items.statement: For signup → search → booking, report the distinct users reaching each step plus the conversion percent between consecutive steps.
hints: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts) as step_rank

items.title: Two-Dimension CUBE
items.statement: CUBE(revenue by country and device) with the GROUPING() mask so margins (country-only, device-only, grand total) are identifiable and ordered.
hints: GROUPING(country), GROUPING(device) to tag margin rows

items.title: Pivot Cohort Sizes
items.statement: Turn a row-per-cohort-day counts table into a matrix with cohort as rows and cohort-day-index as columns (d0..d3) using CASE aggregation.
hints: One SUM(CASE WHEN days_since = 0 THEN cnt END) per target column

revisionCard: GROUPING(col)=1 marks rollup/cube subtotal rows where col was collapsed — the only safe NULL discriminator
GROUPING SETS (explicit) vs ROLLUP (hierarchy) vs CUBE (every combination); one pass in the planner
Share-of-total trick: the window re-sums the grouped aggregate — SUM(SUM(amount)) OVER () = grand total
Retention keys on first activity (MIN(order_date) per user); every later period divides survivors by that cohort size
Funnel = per-user rank of ordered step events, aggregated to the deepest step reached

glossary.def: One combination of grouping columns requested for subtotal rows, e.g. (region) inside a multi-level GROUP BY.
Hierarchical grouping shorthand: (a, b) → (a) → (), one subtotal level per column.
Every subset combination of the grouped columns, margins included.
GROUPING(col) returns 1 when col is collapsed by a rollup/cube, distinguishing subtotal NULLs from real NULLs.
A group of users sharing a first-activity period (e.g. first purchase month).
Share of a cohort still active in a later period: survivors / cohort_size.
Ordered step sequence counted per user along one path (view → cart → purchase).
value / SUM(value) OVER () — each row as a fraction of the grand total.
